title: Cosanima 1.0 documentation
goal: Deliver the Cosanima 1.0 documentation set for the flag-day: user docs (graph concept, quickstart/tutorial, CLI reference for cosanima scan + query), the published versioned frontend-contract reference, the committed-docs policy (SPEC.md + CHANGELOG), an apg → cosanima migration note, and consistent README/docs across the seven really-knows-ai repos.

title: Contract reference + committed docs + migration note
User guide: graph concept + quickstart/tutorial
body: User-facing guide, committed markdown in the core repo at v1.0.0. It leads with the concept that cosanima produces 'a map you navigate' — modules, files, types, functions plus the intent graph (specs/plans/notes/decisions) as native nodes — not a raw graph data structure; the 'map you navigate' framing is the leading metaphor the docs teach. It then walks a quickstart (install → `cosanima init` → `cosanima scan` → `cosanima query`) on a real sample repo and a tutorial with worked examples that read scan output and run common queries.

title: Versioned contract reference published
body: Publish the JSONL schema + FQN rules as the versioned contract reference document — the 'promoted to a versioned cross-repo contract' artifact (cosanima-repo-split R3) given a published home. A committed, revisioned reference in the core repo at v1.0.0 documenting every record/edge type (schema.rs Record/edge records incl. code_type classification and lang_switch) and the FQN rules (module/struct/function/overload rendering + disambiguation, per ingest.rs render_function_fqns). Versioned by the schema revision — conceptually distinct from the CLI semver (consumes cosanima-frontend-interface R8) — and linked from the core README and all six frontend READMEs so frontend authors build against the published contract.

title: Committed-docs policy executed: SPEC.md + CHANGELOG
body: Execute the committed-docs policy as part of the docs set: SPEC.md and CHANGELOG.md are authored, committed at the v1.0.0 tag in the core repo, and kept current — the CHANGELOG covers the 0.9 → 1.0.0 history (rename, license, split, frontend contract, CI) and SPEC.md documents the stable surface. The docs project owns the authoring/currency of these two committed docs; the flag-day gate that they exist as part of the stable surface lives in the parent (cosanima-1.0 R9), which depends on this requirement — referenced there, executed here, not duplicated.

summary: Docs ship as committed markdown in-repo: user docs + the contract reference live in the core repo (README + docs/), each frontend repo carries its own README; there is no separate docs website/hosting for 1.0 (the committed-docs policy is the delivery mechanism).

The contract reference document is the published home of the 'promoted to a versioned cross-repo contract' artifact (cosanima-repo-split R3): it is versioned by the schema revision — conceptually distinct from the CLI semver (cosanima-frontend-interface R8) — committed in the core repo at v1.0.0, and linked from all seven repos.

The apg → cosanima migration note is manual guidance only — no scripts or automation — consistent with the rename's clean cut (no back-compat shims, cosanima-rename D2) and the parent's no-migration-tooling non-goal (cosanima-1.0 ng-4); existing apg users re-init with cosanima following the note's old → new mapping.

English-only docs, and no per-language frontend authoring tutorials for 1.0: frontends get a consistent README plus the contract reference; deep per-language frontend-building guides are post-1.0. [autonomous — no localization or per-language tutorial scope in the brief]

Verification: a pre-1.0 apg user with an existing `apg/` install follows the migration note and lands on a working cosanima setup (re-init under `.cosanima/`) without running any automated migration.

Cosanima-docs is a child of the 1.0 flag-day release (parent cosanima-1.0 SpecDependsOn cosanima-docs): the documentation set is one of the deliverables gated at the v1.0.0 tags. It coordinates the three specs whose work the docs describe — cosanima-rename (the name/commands/layout the docs use), cosanima-repo-split (the seven repos the docs live across), and cosanima-frontend-interface (the contract reference the docs publish) — and executes the committed-docs deliverable the parent rules (R9). Everything is named per the binding Cosanima decision.

The user docs lead with the product framing that gives the rename its reason: cosanima produces 'a map you navigate' — the graph is the active knowledge that drives a program (code + intent/why + trajectory/what's-next as native nodes), not a raw data structure. Every tutorial/worked-example path (scan → query → reading the graph) is taught through that metaphor.

Cross-spec wiring: cosanima-docs SpecDependsOn cosanima-repo-split, cosanima-rename, and cosanima-frontend-interface (docs live across the split repos, use the new name, publish the contract reference); the parent cosanima-1.0 SpecDependsOn cosanima-docs so the flag-day gate includes the docs deliverable. Requirement-level: R3 consumes cosanima-frontend-interface/R8 (schema-revision versioning), R6 consumes cosanima-repo-split/R7 (seven repos with docs ported), R4 is consumed by parent cosanima-1.0/R9 (the committed-docs gate depends on the docs-project authoring), and R5/R6 coordinate in prose with rename D2/R12 and parent ng-4.

source: the brief says the committed-docs requirement 'coordinates with parent cosanima-1.0 R9 — the parent's R9 and this requirement should reference each other rather than duplicate; add a DependsOn or cross-reference'. inconsistency: duplicating R9's body in R4 would fork the stable-surface committed-docs gate across two specs, and a docs→parent requirement edge would point against the spec-level dependency direction (parent SpecDependsOn docs). resolution: R4 owns the authoring/currency of SPEC.md + CHANGELOG.md and references R9 in prose; the parent's R9 keeps the stable-surface gate and gains a requirement-level DependsOn onto cosanima-docs/R4, mirroring the spec-level direction — one artifact, one gate, one ownership [autonomous].

source: the brief asks for 'an apg → cosanima migration note for the (small) pre-1.0 install base, given the rename ships no back-compat shims'. inconsistency: 'migration note' could be read as permission for migration tooling/scripts, which the parent rules out (cosanima-1.0 ng-4: no migration tooling/path — users re-init with cosanima) and the rename's clean cut reinforces (no shims). resolution: R5 + D3 + ng-2 scope the deliverable to a manual-guidance note (old → new mapping + re-init path) with no scripts or automation, so the docs child does not contradict the parent non-goal it coordinates with [autonomous].

title: CLI reference: cosanima scan + query + mcp (incl. cross-harness agents)
body: Authoritative CLI reference for the primary data commands after the rename, matching the shipped v1.0.0 binary: `cosanima scan` (language auto-detect, --language/--module/--exclude-path/blacklist, the scan pipeline, .trans outputs db.lbug + graph.jsonl + cosanima-frontend.log), `cosanima query` (Cypher MATCH/RETURN over db.lbug, CSV output with header), and `cosanima mcp` (the local MCP server: how to run it, stdio transport, which tools/resources it exposes, and how a harness connects to it per cosanima-mcp). The reference also covers the cross-harness agents (the six canonical agents and their harness locations per cosanima-mcp). It does NOT document the retired opencode tool suite as current — the 46 apg_* scripts are gone (replaced by MCP tools) and no cosanima_* script names appear. Covers flags, arguments, output shape, exit codes, and env/config interplay (COSANIMA_FRONTEND_DIR, cosanima/config.json code_type classification). Grounded in the real command implementations (apg.main dispatch → apg.cmd_scan / apg.cmd_query) and rendered under the post-rename names; every example reproduces actual v1.0.0 output.

title: apg → cosanima migration note (tool suite retired → MCP)
body: Publish an apg → cosanima migration note for the deliberately small pre-1.0 install base. Because the rename is a clean cut with no back-compat shims (cosanima-rename D2) and the parent rules no migration tooling (cosanima-1.0 ng-4), the note is manual guidance only — no scripts or automation: what changed (command `cosanima`, data dir `.cosanima/` + `.trans/` artifacts, config at `.cosanima/config.json`, env COSANIMA_FRONTEND_DIR, the opencode tool-suite apg_* RETIRED — replaced by the local MCP server + cross-harness agents per cosanima-mcp — agent prefixes apg_ → cosanima_, spec/plan JSONL roots) and the re-init path from an existing `apg/` install to a working cosanima setup (init now installs the MCP server + cross-harness agents).

title: README + docs consistent across the seven repos (MCP + cross-harness agents)
body: At v1.0.0 all seven really-knows-ai repos carry READMEs (and per-repo docs) that are ported and mutually consistent: identical branding (Cosanima under really-knows-ai), per-repo install/build instructions (core: binary + formula/installer + the local MCP server and cross-harness agent artifacts per cosanima-mcp; each frontend: native build + its formula), the stable-surface stances (Apache-2.0, macOS/Linux platforms, C++ best-effort vs exact edges), and links to the user docs + contract reference. The READMEs do NOT document the retired opencode tool suite as current (no apg_* or cosanima_* tool scripts — agents connect via the MCP server). Consumes cosanima-repo-split R7 ('repos created with docs ported'), which this requirement completes on the docs side; coordinates with the rename's README/docs sweep (cosanima-rename R12) so no live `apg` command/binary instruction remains in any repo's README at the tag (historical/changelog mentions allowed).

source: R2 'CLI reference: cosanima scan + cosanima query' documented only the two primary data commands. inconsistency: the binding architecture decision makes the local MCP server (`cosanima mcp`) and the cross-harness agents 1.0 deliverables (cosanima-mcp), and the opencode tool suite is RETIRED — the docs must document the new surface and must not document the retired tool suite as current. resolution: R2 rephrased — the CLI reference now also covers `cosanima mcp` (run/connect, stdio, tools/resources) and the cross-harness agents, and explicitly excludes the retired apg_*/cosanima_* tool scripts [with user].

source: R5 'apg → cosanima migration note' mapped the tool-suite change as 'tool-suite apg_* → cosanima_*' in the old → new mapping. inconsistency: the MCP decision retires the tool suite (cosanima-mcp D2) — there is no cosanima_* tool-suite rename to document; the mapping would describe a rename that never happens. resolution: R5 rephrased — the 'what changed' list now reads 'the opencode tool-suite apg_* is RETIRED, replaced by the local MCP server + cross-harness agents (cosanima-mcp); agent prefixes apg_ → cosanima_'; the re-init path notes that init installs the MCP server + cross-harness agents [with user].
